docs.title: Report
docs.text: The Report section represents the final step in the data processing workflow. It involves generating a report that consolidates the results of the diffraction data analysis, providing a comprehensive overview of the model refinement process and its outcomes.

docs.title: Contents of the Report
docs.text:
The report includes key details such as:

  • Final refined model parameters – Optimized crystallographic and instrumental parameters.
  • Goodness-of-fit indicators – Metrics such as R-factors, chi-square (χ²), and residuals.
  • Graphical representation – Visualization of experimental vs. calculated diffraction patterns.

docs.title: Saving the Report
docs.text:
Reports are written to disk rather than printed. Call a per-format method directly, or enable formats on project.report (see below) so the next project.save() writes them:

# Write an HTML report immediately
project.report.save_html()

docs.title: Configuring Saved Reports
docs.text:
Report output is controlled by project.report, a project-level configuration category that is saved in project.cif. Regular project.save() calls read this configuration and write the selected report formats.

Setting Type Meaning project.report.cif bool Write an IUCr submission CIF. project.report.html bool Write an HTML report (enabled by default). project.report.tex bool Write a TeX report bundle. project.report.pdf bool Write a PDF report when a TeX engine is available. project.report.html_offline bool Embed HTML assets instead of using CDN links.

HTML output is enabled by default, so saving a project always writes an HTML report unless you set project.report.html = False. Enable additional formats through their boolean flags:

project.report.cif = True
project.save()

This writes reports/<project>.html (enabled by default) and reports/<project>.cif inside the project directory.

When pdf is enabled but tex is not, the intermediate reports/tex/ bundle is written only to build the PDF and removed once the PDF is produced. It is kept if no TeX engine is available so you can compile it by hand.

docs.title: One-Off Report Saves
docs.text:
Per-format methods write a report without changing the saved configuration:

project.report.save_html()
project.report.save_cif()
project.report.save_tex()
project.report.save_pdf()

save_pdf() always writes the TeX bundle first. If no TeX engine is on PATH, EasyDiffraction leaves the .tex and data/ files under reports/tex/, prints a short install hint, and does not raise.

HTML reports load Plotly and MathJax from CDNs by default. Set project.report.html_offline = True to make the HTML report usable without network access; this embeds Plotly in the HTML and copies the vendored MathJax bundle next to it, adding about 4.5 MB total.

The command line saves reports from the persisted project configuration when a fit writes the project back to disk:

python -m easydiffraction path/to/project fit

If project.cif contains _report.html true, _report.tex true, or another enabled report flag, fit writes those reports as part of the normal project save. Use the Python per-format methods above for one-off exports without changing the saved configuration.

Now that the initial user guide is complete, you can explore the EasyDiffraction API for detailed information on the available classes and methods. Additionally, you can find practical examples and step-by-step guides in the Tutorials.

docs.title: diffrn radiation
docs.text: coreCIF

docs.title: _diffrn_radiation
docs.text: Data items in this category describe the radiation used in measuring the diffraction intensities. Please see the IUCr page for further details.

docs.title: _diffrn_radiation.probe
docs.text:
The nature of the radiation used (i.e. the name of the subatomic particle or the region of the electromagnetic spectrum).

Supported values: neutron and x-ray

docs.title: diffrn radiation wavelength
docs.text: coreCIF

docs.title: _diffrn_radiation_wavelength
docs.text: Data items in this category describe the wavelength of radiation used in diffraction measurements. Please see the IUCr page for further details.

docs.title: _diffrn_radiation_wavelength.wavelength
docs.text: Wavelength of the radiation used to measure the unit cell.

docs.title: exptl crystal
docs.text: customCIF

docs.title: extinction
docs.text: customCIF

docs.title: pd calib
docs.text: customCIF

docs.title: _pd_calib
docs.text: This section defines the parameters used for the calibration of the instrument, similar to this IUCr section.

docs.title: _pd_calib.2theta_offset
docs.text: An offset angle (in degrees) used to calibrate 2θ.

docs.title: Atom site
docs.text: coreCIF

docs.title: _atom_site
docs.text: Data items in this category record details about the atom sites in a crystal structure, such as the positional coordinates and atomic displacement parameters. Please see the IUCr page for further details.

docs.title: _atom_site.label
docs.text: This is a unique identifier for a particular site in the asymmetric unit of the crystal unit cell.

docs.title: _atom_site.type_symbol
docs.text: A code to identify the atom specie(s) occupying this site.

docs.title: _atom_site.fract
docs.text:
Atom-site coordinates as fractions of the _cell_length values.

  • _atom_site.fract_x
  • _atom_site.fract_y
  • _atom_site.fract_z

docs.title: _atom_site.occupancy
docs.text: The fraction of the atom type present at this site.

docs.title: _atom_site.ADP_type
docs.text: Code for type of atomic displacement parameters used for the site. Currently only Biso (isotropic B) is supported.

docs.title: _atom_site.B_iso_or_equiv
docs.text: Isotropic atomic displacement parameter, or equivalent isotropic atomic displacement parameter, in angstroms squared.

docs.title: _atom_site.site_symmetry_multiplicity
docs.text:
optional parameter

The number of different sites that are generated by the application of the space-group symmetry to the coordinates given for this site. It is equal to the multiplicity given for this Wyckoff site in International Tables for Crystallography Vol. A (2002).

docs.title: _atom_site.Wyckoff_symbol
docs.text:
optional parameter

The Wyckoff symbol (letter) as listed in the space-group tables of International Tables for Crystallography Vol. A.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: pdCIF

docs.title: _pd_background
docs.text: This category defines various background functions that could be used when calculating diffractograms. Please see the IUCr page for further details.

docs.title: _pd_background.line_segment_X
docs.text:
List of X-coordinates used to create many straight-line segments representing the background in a calculated diffractogram.

Supported values: 2theta and time-of-flight

docs.title: _pd_background.line_segment_intensity
docs.text: List of intensities used to create many straight-line segments representing the background in a calculated diffractogram.

docs.title: _pd_background.X_coordinate
docs.text: The type of X-coordinate against which the pd_background values were calculated.

docs.title: Cell
docs.text: coreCIF

docs.title: _cell
docs.text: Data items in this category record details about the crystallographic cell parameters and their measurement. Please see the IUCr page for further details.

docs.title: _cell.angle
docs.text:
The angles between the bounding cell axes in degrees.

  • _cell.angle_alpha
  • _cell.angle_beta
  • _cell.angle_gamma

docs.title: _cell.length
docs.text:
The lengths of each cell axis in angstroms.

  • _cell.length_a
  • _cell.length_b
  • _cell.length_c

docs.title: Expt type
docs.text: customCIF

docs.title: _expt_type
docs.text: This EasyDiffraction category records the experiment type. The type selects compatible experiment categories, calculators, peak profiles, and data handling.

docs.title: _expt_type.beam_mode
docs.text: Beam mode used by the experiment. Supported values include constant wavelength and time-of-flight.

docs.title: _expt_type.radiation_probe
docs.text: Radiation probe used by the experiment. Supported values include neutron and x-ray.

docs.title: _expt_type.sample_form
docs.text: Sample form used by the experiment. Supported values include powder and single crystal.

docs.title: _expt_type.scattering_type
docs.text: Scattering type used by the experiment. Supported values include bragg and total.

docs.title: Instrument
docs.text: customCIF

docs.title: _instr
docs.text: This category stores instrument setup and calibration parameters used by EasyDiffraction experiments. Constant-wavelength and time-of-flight experiments use different subsets of the category.

docs.title: _instr.wavelength
docs.text:
Incident neutron or X-ray wavelength for constant-wavelength experiments. In Python this is accessed as:

experiment.instrument.setup_wavelength

docs.title: _instr.2theta_offset
docs.text:
Two-theta zero offset for constant-wavelength powder experiments. In Python this is accessed as:

experiment.instrument.calib_twotheta_offset

docs.title: _instr.2theta_bank
docs.text:
Detector-bank two-theta angle for time-of-flight powder experiments. In Python this is accessed as:

experiment.instrument.setup_twotheta_bank

docs.title: _instr.d_to_tof
docs.text:
Time-of-flight calibration terms converting d-spacing to time of flight. In Python these are accessed as:

  • experiment.instrument.calib_d_to_tof_recip
  • experiment.instrument.calib_d_to_tof_offset
  • experiment.instrument.calib_d_to_tof_linear
  • experiment.instrument.calib_d_to_tof_quad

They serialize to the following CIF tags:

  • _instr.d_to_tof_recip
  • _instr.d_to_tof_offset
  • _instr.d_to_tof_linear
  • _instr.d_to_tof_quad

docs.title: Linked phases
docs.text: pdCIF

docs.title: _pd_phase_block
docs.text: A table of phases relevant to the current data block. Each phase is identified by its data block identifier. Please see the IUCr page for further details.

docs.title: _pd_phase_block.id
docs.text: A block ID code identifying a block containing phase information.

docs.title: _pd_phase_block.scale
docs.text: Phase scale.

docs.title: Pd meas
docs.text: pdCIF

docs.title: _pd_meas
docs.text: This section contains the measured diffractogram, similar to this IUCr section.

docs.title: _pd_meas.2theta_scan
docs.text: 2θ diffraction angle (in degrees) for intensity points measured in a scanning method.

docs.title: _pd_meas.time-of-flight
docs.text: Measured time (in microseconds) for time-of-flight neutron measurements.

docs.title: _pd_meas.intensity_total
docs.text: Intensity recorded at each measurement point as a function of angle.

docs.title: _pd_meas.intensity_total_su
docs.text: Standard uncertainty of _pd_meas.2theta_scan.

docs.title: Peak
docs.text: customCIF

docs.title: _peak
docs.text:
This category stores peak-profile parameters used by powder diffraction and total-scattering calculations. The active peak-profile category is selected from the experiment:

experiment.peak.type = 'pseudo-voigt'

docs.title: Constant-wavelength powder profiles
docs.text:
The constant-wavelength pseudo-Voigt profile uses Gaussian and Lorentzian broadening parameters:

  • _peak.broad_gauss_u
  • _peak.broad_gauss_v
  • _peak.broad_gauss_w
  • _peak.broad_lorentz_x
  • _peak.broad_lorentz_y

When empirical asymmetry is enabled, the profile also uses:

  • _peak.asym_p1
  • _peak.asym_p2
  • _peak.asym_p3
  • _peak.asym_p4

docs.title: Time-of-flight powder profiles
docs.text:
The time-of-flight pseudo-Voigt profiles use instrument-dependent Gaussian broadening, back-to-back exponential rise and decay terms, and optionally Lorentzian broadening or double-exponential asymmetry terms:

  • _peak.gauss_sigma_0
  • _peak.gauss_sigma_1
  • _peak.gauss_sigma_2
  • _peak.rise_alpha_0
  • _peak.rise_alpha_1
  • _peak.decay_beta_0
  • _peak.decay_beta_1
  • _peak.lorentz_gamma_0
  • _peak.lorentz_gamma_1
  • _peak.lorentz_gamma_2
  • _peak.dexp_rise_alpha_1
  • _peak.dexp_rise_alpha_2
  • _peak.dexp_decay_beta_00
  • _peak.dexp_decay_beta_01
  • _peak.dexp_decay_beta_10

docs.title: Total-scattering profiles
docs.text:
Total-scattering peak parameters describe Q-space cutoff, broadening, sharpening, and damping:
